item.title: Current Operational Zones
item.content:encoded:
X1 is N and S America. Currently irradiated after the thermonuclear bombing.

Great Britain (Probably X2) is currently destroyed in its entirety after a 173 sighting and subsequent scorched earth thermonuclear strike.

Presumably, there is nowhere else left to go. With this large of a containment perimeter plus the gap that was the British Isles, it's probably safe to assume complete failure of containment, and subsequent overrunning of all remaining areas.

Along with that, the moon is completely gone, and the only option at this point would be to evacuate all the people left and Exterminatus the planet with an AM bomb or something after leaving for Mars.

item.title: MULTI NUTS
item.content:encoded: Honestly already not a fan of the idea and it feels like a sort of fan-fiction. No explanation for why they multiply and it's not the type of mystery that actually intrigues you, but more just the type of mystery that feels like it's just there. The one thing I like about it though, is that it's different from the normal "WORLD IS DESTROYED BY CRAZY EXTRADIMENSIONAL GOD." It can't really fit into any headcanons and feels more like a joke. Honestly, I hate it when an SCP just randomly kills 682 because it's SUPER STRONG. I'll give you this though, it's pretty hilarious.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thing is: Nothing is said about it in the original article. Furthermore, gunfire is about the least effective way to contain something like 173 and the Foundation, including its assets (MTFs), wouldn't even try it if we think about for a second, unless they were actively trying to actively neutralize it.

Problem with articles such as 173 and 682 is that they are a product from a different time and their containment procedures hardly ever measure up to what we'd expect nowadays - put either into a fancy\sturdy enough box, and they'd be about the last anomalies you'd expect a breach from.

Exactly what makes it appealing, IMO, is how ordinary it is: 173 is just another number for something terrifying into a terrifying universe, where there's a facility somewhere keeping tabs on a statue that bleeds and shits as if that was a common desk job.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nothing in the original article suggests the statue to be anomalously durable. For all we know, it IS just rock, concrete and rebar, which you can smash just fine.

173 poses a massive threat in this tale because not only can it multiply itself at an alarming rate but these additional instances also have such high intelligence that they capable of cooperation between themselves to systematically breach containment.

The whole scenario, however, only escalates because A: Plot convenience or\and B: Author's headcanon of the Foundation. As popular articles such as 354 and 871 show, no, the Foundation isn't dogmatically opposed to destroying new instances of something if they pose significant danger or even heightened difficulty of containment.
